What an aerial actually proves in Grandville

Grandville is the established southwest suburb buyers pick when they want a settled, family-focused community with everyday convenience built in. RiverTown Crossings anchors the area as a regional retail hub and I-196 puts downtown Grand Rapids minutes away. Grandville listings sell on the settled-family lifestyle.

An aerial frame is the only one that shows the wooded Buck Creek buffer, the trail access, and how a lot sits relative to schools and parks — the three things Grandville buyers are actually paying a premium for. That is the whole argument for drone here: it is not a prettier photo, it is a different piece of information. A buyer scrolling a gallery on their phone can read a lot line, a tree canopy, or a five-minute commute in one frame, and cannot read any of it from a front elevation.

Grandville airspace: what actually applies

Grandville sits near Gerald R. Ford International Airport (KGRR), so parts of the city fall inside the FAA LAANC grid. That is not a blocker — it means authorization has to be filed before the flight where the grid requires it, and the ceiling confirmed for the specific address.

Practically, that means authorization is required on part of the map here. Every ECS flight is flown by a Part 107 certified Remote Pilot in Command, the airspace is checked against the FAA UAS facility map for your specific address before the shoot, and authorization is filed in advance where the grid calls for it. The flight is planned before the shoot day, not improvised in the driveway. For the full rundown see drone laws for Grand Rapids real estate agents.

How the flight is run

The aerial is captured during the same visit as the HDR stills, so there is no second appointment and no second invoice. Standard coverage is a set of context frames at varying altitude and angle: a high overhead that reads as a lot map, a mid-altitude three-quarter that shows the home in the neighborhood, and a low approach that keeps the architecture the subject. Weather calls are made the morning of, and a scrubbed flight moves rather than becoming a rushed one in bad light.

Delivery is the same as the rest of the shoot: edited and back to you the next business day, sized for MLS and for social.

Grandville drone photography FAQ

Do you need LAANC authorization to fly a drone in Grandville?
Grandville sits near Gerald R. Ford International Airport (KGRR), so parts of the city fall inside the FAA LAANC grid. That is not a blocker — it means authorization has to be filed before the flight where the grid requires it, and the ceiling confirmed for the specific address. We handle the filing before the shoot, so the answer for an agent is simply yes, it is covered.

How much does drone photography cost for a Grandville listing?
$125 added to an Essential ($245) or Showcase ($375) package, and included at no extra cost in Signature ($525).

Is the drone pilot licensed?
Yes. Every flight is flown by an FAA Part 107 certified Remote Pilot in Command. Commercial real estate drone work without Part 107 is not legal, and it is a fair question to ask any photographer before you hire them.

How fast do I get the aerials back?
Next business day, the same as the rest of the shoot. Aerials for Grandville listings are delivered edited and MLS-ready alongside the interiors and exteriors.
